summary: Some Old Stuff (S.O.S) is a Game Boy Color demo by R-Lab released in 2000, with code by Quant and Dark, graphics by Juge and Dark, and music by DNK and Dark.
why: A Game Boy Color demo from 2000 that collects R-Lab's earlier material, which makes it a look at the group's work on the handheld at the turn of the century.

summary: Hooy-Program and Raww Arse's ZX Spectrum 48K demo that won the ZX Spectrum demo compo at Forever 2001, with code by Gasman, a large graphics team and a guest part by ZeroTeam.
why: It won its compo at Forever 2001, and it pulls together work from several Spectrum artists and musicians. It's also tagged for using the Spectrum's multicolour mode.

summary: A 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Software Failure, with code, graphics and music all by Ham. It placed 4th in the Open Intro compo at Euskal 2024.
why: A one-person production squeezed into 16K that held its own in a mixed-platform intro compo at Euskal 2024.

summary: Atari 8-bit demo by New Generation and Zelax, built around a robot theme, which came second in the Atari Demo compo at Forever 2023.
why: A runner-up at Forever 2023 from a large joint crew, with kris3d credited for the idea and 3D graphics and music from ZoltarX, Tatqoo, LiSU and Miker.

summary: Genesis Project's one-file C64 demo built around a graffiti theme: a big Genesis Project logo by Alien with a spray-can scroller painting text beneath it, to a hip-hop tune by MCH. Placed 3rd in C64 Demo at Demo of the Year 2014.
why: Sceners single out the spray-paint scroller and how well MCH's music suits the theme, calling the whole thing a stylish little package with plenty of attitude.

quote.text: Everything fits together, with a badass attitude. Really cool.

summary: Desire's 8K intro for the C64, coded by Daison with music by No-XS, a big graffiti-style logo by BokanoiD and a charset by Hammerfist. It came third in the Intro Creation Competition 2013.
why: Sceners single out the logo, praised for being pixelled without heavy dithering, and the way Daison makes simple FLD bouncing look like an Amiga intro.

quote.text: Wow.. the logo is impressive .. another excellent example to pixel without too much dithering. top notch!

summary: Light's C64 demo that took second place in the C64 demo compo at The Party 1994, with code by Yabba, Flamingo and Waco and music by Rob Hubbard and Martin Galway.
why: Sceners single out how complex and fast the effects were for 1994, especially the raytracer, the bezier curve morph and the multicolour Doom-style 3D part at the end.

quote.text: Looking at the year (94) it's hard to believe the complexity and speed of the effects.

summary: A cracktro-style Amstrad CPC prod by Vanity, with code by Hicks, graphics by Beb and Targhan's remix of the Saboteur 2 music. It came 2nd in the combined demo/intro compo at ReSeT 2018.
why: A second place at ReSeT 2018 from a small team of well-known CPC names. It's a short, single-screen piece worth a look for its split-screen layout.

summary: A Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Legion Of Doom and Absence And Wilds, with code and music by Csabo and graphics by Chronos. It took second place in the demo compo at Árok 2011.
why: A Plus/4 take on the Nyan Cat meme that placed second at Árok 2011, made by a small team where Csabo handled both code and music.
highlights: pixelled Nyan Cat with rainbow trail

summary: Onslaught's C64 4K intro, coded by Enthusi with graphics by Veto and music by Conrad, placed 6th in the combined compo at BCC Party 2011. It builds a scrolling picture of a swan entirely from raster splits.
why: Sceners praised it as an original use of raster splits, a new graphics trick the group named "PRS" for permanent raster split. Several compared the blocky look to the Atari 2600, and one called it the highlight of the party.

quote.text: Wow! Beautiful to me, this is probably my fave new gfx mode since interlaced PETSCII.

summary: Crest's 1997 Commodore 64 demo, the follow-up to Krestage, coded by Crossbow with an endpart by The Syndrom and music from Mitch, Dane, The Syndrom and guest JCH/Vibrants.
why: A well-rated Crest demo on CSDb. Sceners single out the intro and the stretching logo, and some still prefer the original Krestage.

quote.text: The intro and logo stretch look very nice.

summary: A 4K intro for the Atari VCS by Tristar and Red Sector Inc., coded by Peiselulli and SvOlli, which placed 4th in the Oldskool 4k compo at Revision 2014.
why: A size-limited intro on the 2600, one of the most constrained machines in the scene, that held its own in an oldskool compo. Its source code is available for anyone curious how it was done.

summary: A one-file Commodore 64 demo from Cosine, coded and drawn by The Magic Roundabout with music by Sack, which came 4th in the Oldskool Demo compo at Sundown 2006.
why: Sceners call it small, simple and stylish: no killer effects, but tidy oldstyle routines, neat pictures by T.M.R and a short lo-fi tune from Sack.

quote.text: Very wonderful, simple but so stylish. More of this, please.

summary: A 16K C64 intro by EXclusive ON, made single-handedly by Jammer (code, graphics, music), placing 5th in the Intro Creation Competition 2016: a big logo over layered raster stripes with a greetings scroller.
why: Jammer's debut as a coder, and sceners were impressed that he wrote his own sample player alongside a funky original track. They also single out the layered raster effect, which one called a tribute to tape-loading stripes.

quote.text: Feels very oldschool yet very fresh at the same time, impressive!

summary: A Commodore 64 demo by Active, coded by Artlace, released at Datastorm 2014 where it placed 14th in the C64 demo compo.
why: A small party demo with a thin record. It's worth a look for its digitised portrait picture and its greetings grid of group names.

summary: Retro Plasma is a Commodore 64 demo by Return, released at 7DX 2011 where it placed 4th in the Demo compo. It runs a blocky colour-cycling plasma behind a checkerboard, with credits for music by Slowhand and logo by Spritus.
why: A small, tidy production that sceners praised for its polish, noting Return seemed to improve with each release.

quote.text: it's just the type of small and polished code I like.

summary: A demo by g0blinish for the ZX Spectrum's TS-Conf enhanced configuration (Pentevo), which won the Low End Enhanced Demo compo at DiHalt 2017 Lite.
why: A compo winner at DiHalt 2017 Lite and a rare example of a demo written for the TS-Conf enhanced Spectrum hardware.

summary: Fatzone's Commodore 64 demo, coded by Pezac and Malmix, which won the Commodore demo compo at Forever 2009. Pezac also wrote the music, Malmix the graphics.
why: It took first place in the Commodore demo competition at Forever 2009. The credits also name a loader by The Dreams and a music player by JCH.

summary: Rainbow is a ZX Spectrum demo by GDC that placed second in the wild demo competition at Riverwash 2016.
why: A podium finish in Riverwash 2016's wild demo compo. The fact sheet has no comments or notes beyond that placing, so the video has to make its own case.

summary: A ZX Spectrum 128K demo by Kpacku, coded by Trefi with graphics by prof4d and Tutty and music by Nik-O. It placed second in the ZX Spectrum demo compo at 3BM OpenAir 2015.
why: A runner-up at 3BM OpenAir 2015 that uses the Spectrum's multicolour mode to push more colour into its artwork than the standard attribute grid allows.

summary: Desire's invitation to Silly Venture 2017 in Gdańsk for the Atari 8-bit, with code by Heaven and Popmilo, graphics by Moonwalker and Veto, and music by Miker. It placed 6th in the 8-bit demo/intro compo at RetroKomp / Load Error 2017.
why: An Atari party invitation made by a full Desire line-up of coders, graphicians and a musician, and it was entered in the RetroKomp / Load Error 2017 8-bit compo.

summary: Michael Park's 1985 Atari 8-bit demo for Xanth F/X: a red-and-white chequered ball bouncing across a teal grid, casting its shadow as it goes.
why: An early answer from the Atari 8-bit to the Amiga's famous Boing Ball demo, showing the older machine could put on the same show. One of the oldest prods on the site.

summary: Desire's Atari 8-bit demo, placed sixth in the Oldskool Demo compo at Revision 2025, with code and graphics by Heaven, graphics by Gaspar, music by mAZE and a 3D engine by Probe.
why: A recent Atari XL/XE entry at Revision with a credited 3D engine from Probe alongside Heaven's code and graphics, placing sixth in a competitive oldskool field.

summary: Iris is a 1997 ZX Spectrum demo by Flash, also credited as Flash Inc in the video title.
why: A late-90s Spectrum demo with no compo record. Worth a look for anyone exploring the Spectrum scene of that era.
highlights: dotted line curves in ornate frame

summary: Gasman's ZX Spectrum demo, an invitation to Sundown 2013, which came second in the Oldskool Demo compo at Assembly 2013. Chunky, dithered pictures sit above a text scroller.
why: A runner-up at Assembly's oldskool compo, and an invitation intro on a stock 48K Spectrum with AY music.

summary: Faque's one-file Commodore 64 demo from 1999, which came second in the C64 demo compo at Mekka & Symposium 1999.
why: Sceners point to the code: an animated raytraced shadows effect and an interference part, which one commenter rated good for 1999 and still spectacular years later.

quote.text: good code for 99 but even spectacular today, the raytrace stuff is animated.

summary: A 256-byte tunnel intro for the Atari Lynx by 42Bastian, placed third in the 256-Byte Intro compo at Sommarhack 2020. The video title puts it at 249 bytes.
why: Nominated for Best Oldschool Tiny Intro at The Nano Awards 2021, and a rare tiny intro on the Lynx. The source code is available.

summary: Offence's one-file C64 demo from December 2018, a tribute to BHF/Abnormal, who died that April. Pal's portrait of Bård sits beside messages from his friends, with code by Perplex and music by GT.
why: Sceners call it a heartfelt tribute where everything feels right, and single out GT's soundtrack of more than ten minutes, especially its SID guitar solo, as one of the finest C64 tunes.

quote.text: This is a really emotional tribute and everything seems just right - coding, phenomenal music, mood and texts.

summary: Impact's Amstrad Plus demo from 2023, coded and drawn by Kris with music by Pator, opening on a grim reaper title screen.
why: A recent one-person code-and-graphics showcase for the Plus hardware, with a soundtrack by Pator. It went down well on Pouët.

summary: A 16K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Impact, released in 2021.
why: A thin fact sheet, but the title suggests pictures built from triangles, and the stills bear that out with flat-shaded geometric images.

summary: A Commodore 64 intro by Genesis Project, with code, music and graphics all by Mermaid, that came 4th in the Intro Creation Competition 2016. Shaded bubbles drift around big Genesis Project logos above a scroller.
why: Sceners single out the graphics: logos built from multicolour sprites with a hires character overlay, and shaded bubbles mixing multicolour and hires. Several commenters say it has an Amiga feel, and coders expected the technique to be copied.

quote.text: Absolutely brilliant use of hires and multicolor. Thanks for sharing the behind-the-scenes screenshots. Totally blows me on how beautiful this looks.

summary: Finnish Gold's C64 demo, first shown at Zoo 2019 where it placed 5th, then released in its complete 100% version two years later, winning the combined demo compo at Saunasolmu 2021.
why: A long-gestating group effort with code, music and graphics by Proton, plus logos by Pal and Shine. The finished version took first place at Saunasolmu 2021.

summary: Bonzai's two-disk, James Bond-themed C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Gubbdata 2022: a run of scroller parts with graphics by Facet, The Sarge, Dize and Fox and music by DRAX, Laxity and Metal.
why: Sceners praise how it pulls off its effects while sticking to one theme, with Facet and The Sarge's graphics and the Bond-flavoured music singled out, along with the comic James Band part.

quote.text: I am deeply impressed by how you pull off all the effects while sticking to one chosen theme, which was James Bond this time.

summary: A three-screen oldschool C64 demo by Noice, released in 2011, styled after early-90s demos: big colourful logos, scrollers and sprite effects, with logos by Rocket.
why: Sceners welcomed it as oldschool done properly, praising the effects, the logo design and the flying logo in the first part. Comments also mention it set a record, with Axis and Cruzer promising to beat it.
highlights: flying logo in the first part

quote.text: finally someone not using oldschool as an excuse for being lame :) very nice.

summary: A ZX Spectrum birthday intro by Togyaf, released in September 2011 as a gift.
why: A small personal prod from the Spectrum scene, made as a birthday present and worth a look as an example of the scene's gift-intro tradition.

summary: A Halloween intro for the Amstrad Plus by Impact, with code by Demoniak and graphics by Kris. It placed 2nd in the combined demo/intro compo at Benediction Coding Party #4 2024.
why: A seasonal piece that took second place at Benediction Coding Party #4, made by a two-person team of coder and graphician.

summary: Atari Programming Champions' Atari 8-bit demo from 1994, coded by Little Beatle Software with music by Marucha and graphics by Dave. It won the demo compo at Shadows Copy Party 1994.
why: A compo winner from the mid-1990s Atari 8-bit scene, tagged as a dentro and built around shade-bob effects.

summary: An Atari 8-bit demo by Raster of Computer Platform Unlimited, who did both the code and the music. It won the Atari Demo competition at Forever 2004.
why: A compo winner at Forever 2004, and a one-man production with Raster handling both code and soundtrack.

summary: Contrast's 1993 Amstrad CPC demo, coded by Gozeur with graphics by ZZ Top and music by Ric: a full-screen colour plasma above a control panel, with a large scrolling message underneath.
why: A thin fact sheet, but a tidy single-effect CPC demo from 1993 with an original soundtrack by Ric, uploaded by its coder Gozeur.

summary: A New Year 2015 intro for the Atari 8-bit from Desire, with code by Heaven, graphics by Alien and music by Triace. A large logo sits above a fire effect, with a mirrored scroller underneath.
why: A small seasonal greeting from Desire, made by an established Atari XL trio and released on New Year's Day 2015. It's a short, easy watch rather than a compo entry.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by PMWD, with code and design by 0xF and music by Ryxa. It won the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2003.
why: A compo winner in one of the tightest size categories, fitting both visuals and Ryxa's music into a kilobyte.

summary: A one-screen C64 demo by Chorus, coded by Clarence with music by DRAX: a band of dense, moving raster-split patterns above a scroller and a colourful Chorus logo. It won the C64 Demo category of Demo of the Year 2014.
why: Sceners were baffled by how the dense colour splits were done, and debated FLI, badlines and bank switching for years. Clarence explained it as sine-moved rasterbars drawn into an FLI area. They also praise the colour and pattern choices.

quote.text: Awesome trick! Colors and patterns are also very well selected.

summary: A 4K intro for the Amstrad CPC by Madram, released at Revision 2023 where it placed 6th in the Oldskool 4k Intro competition.
why: A size-limited CPC intro from a strong Revision field. Worth a look for how much imagery Madram fits into 4K.

summary: A 1K intro for the Atari 8-bit by MaPa (code) and PG (music), which came second in the Atari 1K Intro compo at Forever 2013.
why: A runner-up in Forever 2013's Atari 1K compo, fitting both code and music into a single kilobyte.

summary: Monopsy 2 is a Commodore 16/Plus 4 demo by Wilds, released in July 2006. It placed second in the demo competition at Árok 2006.
why: A runner-up at Árok 2006 and a showcase for the Plus 4 scene of the mid-2000s. Worth a look for anyone exploring what the TED machines can do.

summary: Genesis Project's 16K intro for the Atari 8-bit, placed third in the Atari XL/XE 16kb intro compo at Silly Venture 2k19. Code and charset by Shadow, music by MCH, logos by Facet.
why: A small-size compo entry from Genesis Project that placed at Silly Venture, the main Atari 8-bit party.

summary: Padua's Commodore 64 demo, second in the demo compo at Transmission64 2022. Its graphics are built from just five characters, a constraint the Italian title, 'five', hints at.
why: Sceners called it the most original release at the party and praised its minimalist design, its flow and Toggle's music. One commenter found that the idea wore thin without conventional effects.

quote.text: Just takes five to make an awesome demo! Love the approach and minimalistic design!

summary: Fraction's C64 demo that won the C64 demo compo at Rush Hours 1998, with code from six coders and guest graphics from Shell, ALG, Colitt and Talbot, plus music by Kordiaukis.
why: A compo winner at Rush Hours 1998. The disk also carries a note coded by Dux announcing that Shell, Chash and Signor had left for Caution, though Shell's code still made it into the demo.

summary: Benediction's Amstrad CPC demo that won the demo compo at Castellum Secretum 2007, with code and graphics by Krusty and music by PulkoMandy.
why: It took first place in the Castellum Secretum 2007 demo compo, and it's a short, compact piece of work from a two-person Benediction team.

summary: Atlantis's cow-themed C64 demo that won the Oldschool / Alternative Platforms compo at MountainBytes 2023, with code by Honcho, Dr. Science and Maxlide, graphics by Almighty God and Lobo, and music by theK.
why: Sceners call it fresh and single out the opening, a rotating cow, a cow on a motorbike and a 3D dot cow.

quote.text: Yay, this is fresh! I love the beginning, and the rotating cow is really cool!
